To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lowest dose of folic acid that is needed for the mandatory fortification of cereal grain products in order to reduce the incidence of NDTs is 0.1– 0.2 mg/100 g flour, and that the lowest dose that can be expected to reduce the incidence by 50% is 1.0–1.2 mg/ 100 g flour.
mandatory folic acid flour fortification at a level that is currently practiced in the United States (140 mg/ 100 g) is not necessary to prevent NTDs in the general population.

mandatory fortification of wheat flour with 1 mg of folic acid/kg is associated with a substantial increase in folate status in the general population, and the lowest fortification dose that would achieve a similar level of folate status as the current level is approximately 0.3 mg/kg.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mandatory fortification with folic acid has been successful, but there are some uncertainties that need to be resolved before we can conclude that it is safe.
mandatory folic acid supplementation is effective in the prevention of NTDs, but that the optimal dose for this purpose has not yet been determined.

mandatory folic acid supplementation in countries that do not have a high prevalence of NTDs is not justified and should be abandoned, and that countries that have already introduced mandatory folic acid supplements should reconsider their strategy and consider lowering the fortification level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lowest dose of folic acid that can be effective in reducing the risk of NTDs is 0.1 mg/d.

we have shown that there is a large variation in folic acid concentrations in the blood of the general population, which is not only a result of the amount of folic acid intake but also a function of the genetic makeup.

folic acid fortifi cation has reduced the incidence of neural defects, but the benefits of folic acid fortiffcation are not limited to women of reproductive age, and folic acid is not without potential harm to some population segments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lowest possible folic acid fortifi- cation level that is safe and effective in reducing NTDs is not known (9).
the current mandatory fortification of folic acid in North America is likely to be effective at reducing NTDs at a cost of increased risk of masking vitamin B-12 status in the elderly population.
the current mandatory folic acid level in the United States is too high.
